# Dukanipāta (AN 2)
**ID:** AN 2
**Section:** Aṅguttaranikāya (an)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Dukanipāta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/an2

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dukanipāta* ("The Book of the Twos") is the second major division of the *Aṅguttaranikāya*, organizing teachings and doctrinal principles into sets of two [SuttaCentral]. Among its prominent discourses is the *Samacitta Sutta* (AN 2.35/36), delivered by Sāriputta to the "devas of tranquil mind," which addresses the residual rebirths awaiting practitioners at the first three stages of awakening (stream-enterer, once-returner, and non-returner) in either the sensual or higher realms [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. In another discourse, the Buddha designates his two chief disciples, Sāriputta and Mahāmoggallāna, as the exemplar and standard for all ordained monks to emulate (AN 2.131) [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. The collection also records Mahākaccāna's dialogue with the brahmin Kandarāyana (AN 2.38), in which the elder redefines seniority in the noble discipline, asserting that true elderhood stems not from advanced chronological age but from overcoming attachment to sensual pleasures [Nyanaponika et al. 2003].
Numerous discourses in the *Dukanipāta* have preserved parallels in other early Buddhist canons. SuttaCentral identifies curated parallels for 45 suttas, including correspondences in the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125 and T 150A), *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99 and T 100), and *Madhyamāgama* (such as MĀ 21 to AN 2.36 and MĀ 127 to AN 2.35), alongside Sanskrit manuscript fragments cataloged from Turfan and the Schøyen Collection [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus demonstrates massive internal formulaic reuse across 395 Pali texts (14,884 matches), primarily with other numerical divisions of the *Aṅguttaranikāya* (notably AN 4, AN 10, and AN 3) and sections of the *Saṃyuttanikāya* (such as SN 12 and SN 35) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the *Dukanipāta* with Sanskrit fragments of the *Ekottarāgama*, Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣyaṭīkā Upāyikā* (D4094), and Chinese Āgama texts, confirming extensive cross-tradition continuity [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
